transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

I came in because I lost my temper on a board call over a small question about the facility budget. I snapped at someone, and that’s not how I run my company or how I treat people. It bothered me enough that I thought I should talk to somebody.
Has this kind of reaction—losing your temper or feeling overwhelmed—happened before, especially in response to stress or small conflicts?
Not like that, no. I mean, I deal with stress all the time, but snapping on that board call over a small budget question—that felt out of character for me. That’s why it got my attention.
Can you describe how you usually handle conflicts or stress in your personal or professional life? Have you noticed any patterns in how you react emotionally under pressure?

Usually I handle stress pretty directly. I try to stay calm, deal with the issue, make a decision, and move on. I’m not someone who blows up at people.

That’s why the board call bothered me. It was a small question about the facility budget, and I snapped. It wasn’t how I run my company, and it’s not how I treat people.
Have you ever had similar outbursts or reactions in other situations, even if they weren’t related to work or stress?
No, not really. The thing that stands out is that board call. It was a small question about the facility budget, and I just snapped. That’s not normal for me, and it’s not how I want to treat people.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there isn't a specific problem at hand?

I’m not sure I’d say most days. I mean, I worry when there’s something real going on, like work or a problem I need to deal with. But just sitting there anxious for no reason… I haven’t really noticed that as a regular thing.
Have you ever felt a strong urge to lash out or had difficulty controlling your anger in other situations, even if you didn’t actually act on it?

Not really in other situations. The one I keep coming back to is that board call. It was a small question about the facility budget, and I snapped at them. That’s what bothered me, because I don’t run my company that way, and I don’t want to treat people like that.
Outside of that board call, have you noticed that you’ve been more irritable or easily frustrated lately, even over small things?

I haven’t noticed it as a pattern, no. The reason I came in is because I snapped on that board call over a small facility budget question. That really bothered me, because that’s not how I run my company or treat people.
Have you ever had strong emotional reactions or impulsive behaviors in situations involving personal relationships, self-image, or feelings of emptiness, even if it wasn’t about anger?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had normal stress in relationships and work like anyone, but not strong reactions or doing impulsive things because of feeling empty or anything like that. That doesn’t really sound like me.
Since that board call, have you noticed yourself being more irritable or having a shorter temper in other situations, even outside of work stress?
Not really outside of that. The thing that’s been bothering me is still that board call — I snapped over a small facility budget question, and that’s just not how I run my company or treat people.
Have there been times when you felt your emotions were so intense that you acted in ways you later regretted, even if it wasn't about anger or work-related stress?
No, I can’t really think of times like that. I’ve made mistakes and had regrets like anybody, but not because my emotions got so intense that I acted out or did something impulsive.
Since the board call, have you noticed any ongoing feelings of being tense, on edge, or unusually irritable, even when things are calm?

I wouldn’t say it’s been ongoing all the time. The main thing is that board call—I snapped over a small facility budget question, and that really bothered me because that’s not how I run my company or treat people.
Have you ever had episodes of anger or emotional outbursts in personal relationships that seemed out of proportion to the situation, even if you didn’t act on them?

No, not in personal relationships, not that I can point to. What got me here was that board call — I snapped over a small facility budget question, and it bothered me because that’s not how I run my company or treat people.
Have you been dealing with any other stressors or changes in your life recently, outside of that board call?

Not really, no. I mean, nothing major comes to mind outside of that. Life’s always got some pressure with work and day-to-day things, but I haven’t noticed any big change or separate stressor recently.
Have you noticed any days where you feel more irritable or angry than usual, even when there isn’t a specific stressor or problem going on?

Not really as a general thing. The one that stands out is that board call—I got sharp over a small facility budget question, and it bothered me. That’s just not how I try to run my company or treat people.

Have you ever done something on impulse when you weren’t stressed or upset, like making a sudden big decision, spending a lot of money quickly, or acting on a sudden emotion without thinking it through?
No, I don’t think so. I’m usually pretty controlled with decisions—especially money or big commitments. I can’t think of a time I just acted on impulse like that when I wasn’t already upset.
Have you ever had sudden, intense episodes of anger where you felt like you couldn’t control yourself, even if you didn’t act on those feelings?

The only real example I can point to is that board call. I snapped over a small facility budget question, and that bothered me because that’s not how I run my company or how I want to treat people. I wouldn’t say I lost control completely, but it felt sharper than me.
Have you noticed yourself being more irritable, angry, or reactive even during times when things are calm and there isn’t any real stress or problem going on?

I wouldn’t say it happens when things are calm, no. The main thing is still that board call—I snapped over a small facility budget question, and it bothered me because that’s not how I run my company or treat people.
Have you ever had sudden outbursts of emotional distress, such as crying spells or rage, that you felt you couldn't control, even if they weren't directed at others?

I wouldn’t call it crying spells or rage exactly. The thing that stands out is still that board call—I snapped at someone over a small facility budget question, and that’s really not how I run my company or how I want to treat people. It felt out of character for me.
Have you ever had any other episodes, even minor ones, where you felt your emotional reaction was out of character for you, even if you didn’t act on it or it wasn’t directed at others?

Not really any others that come to mind. It’s mainly that board call. I reacted too sharply over a small facility budget question, and it threw me because that’s not how I usually handle people or run things.
